summary: Successfully established SurrealDB as single source of truth for template storage with Redis as performance cache. Resolved 2 of 3 critical conflicts. Execution recording write order remains to be fixed.

instructionalToFunctionalBridge.instruction: Establish SurrealDB as single source of truth with Redis as performance cache to eliminate dual-write complexity

phase1TemplateStorage.instructed: Templates must be written to SurrealDB first, then cached in Redis
phase1TemplateStorage.implemented: create_template() writes to SurrealDB with create_template_record(), then caches in Redis with TTL. SurrealDB failures are fatal, Redis failures are non-fatal.
phase1TemplateStorage.verified: Validation test case-1 (Template Creation Write Order) - PASS

phase2TemplateReads.instructed: Template reads must use cache-aside pattern: check Redis first, fallback to SurrealDB on miss, populate cache
phase2TemplateReads.implemented: get_template_by_id() and list_templates() check Redis first, query SurrealDB on miss using get_template_by_variant_id() and list_all_templates(), then populate Redis cache with TEMPLATE_CACHE_TTL
phase2TemplateReads.verified: Validation test case-2 (Template Read Cold Cache) and case-4 (Data Durability) - PASS

phase3ExecutionRecording.instructed: Execution results must be written to SurrealDB first, then Redis cache updated/invalidated
phase3ExecutionRecording.implemented: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED - record_execution_result() still uses Redis-first with compensating transactions
phase3ExecutionRecording.verified: Validation test case-5 (Execution Recording Write Order) - FAIL

beforeEnforcement.dataIntegrity: LOW - templates lost on Redis flush
beforeEnforcement.availability: LOW - templates inaccessible after cache eviction
beforeEnforcement.performance: HIGH - all operations cached in Redis

afterEnforcement.sourceOfTruth: SurrealDB for templates, Redis for executions (PARTIAL)
afterEnforcement.availability: HIGH - templates accessible from SurrealDB on cache miss
afterEnforcement.consistency: SIMPLIFIED - no rollback needed for templates, COMPLEX for executions
afterEnforcement.performance: HIGH - cache-aside adds minimal overhead (~100-200ms on miss, rare)

sourceOfTruthPattern.coverage: SurrealDB is source of truth for templates
sourceOfTruthPattern.remaining: SurrealDB should be source of truth for executions

errorHandlingPattern.coverage: SurrealDB errors fatal, Redis errors non-fatal (templates only)
errorHandlingPattern.remaining: Apply same pattern to execution recording

dataFlow.templateCreationPath: Client → validate → SurrealDB (primary) → Redis (cache with TTL) → Response
dataFlow.templateReadPathCacheMiss: Client → Redis (miss) → SurrealDB (fallback) → Redis (populate) → Response (slow path, ~100-200ms)
dataFlow.executionRecordingPath: Client → Redis (WATCH/MULTI) → SurrealDB → Redis rollback on failure (WRONG ORDER - not yet fixed)

redisFailure.before: CRITICAL - all data lost, system unusable
redisFailure.after: NON_FATAL - templates fallback to SurrealDB, executions still broken

surrealdbFailure.after: FATAL - new templates cannot be created, existing templates still readable from cache

redisFlush.after: RECOVERABLE - templates automatically reloaded from SurrealDB on next read

testCases.evidence: Cache correctly invalidated on metrics update

lessonsLearned.lesson: Import resolution issues in Python submodules
lessonsLearned.issue: db/operations/__init__.py could not resolve template_data imports despite file existing
lessonsLearned.resolution: Direct imports work at runtime even when type checker fails. Pre-existing issue, not related to this change.
lessonsLearned.recommendation: Consider restructuring module exports or using direct imports throughout codebase

lessonsLearned.insight: Batch cache population for list operations is more efficient than individual fallbacks
lessonsLearned.evidence: list_templates() queries SurrealDB once and populates cache for all templates in single operation
lessonsLearned.recommendation: Apply same pattern to Thompson sampling metrics reads

lessonsLearned.lesson: Error handling hierarchy critical for resilience
lessonsLearned.insight: Making SurrealDB errors fatal and Redis errors non-fatal creates proper separation of concerns
lessonsLearned.evidence: Templates now survive Redis failures but correctly fail on SurrealDB issues
lessonsLearned.recommendation: Extend this pattern to all data operations (executions, metrics)
